Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
620 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Heat Advisory in effect for our southern counties (including the
  City of Houston) through early this evening.  
 
- Frontal boundary may bring isolated showers/storms this
  afternoon and evening.

- While a drop in humidity is expected on Sunday, hot conditions
  are expected with highs in the upper 90s to near 100. Even
  hotter on Monday.
  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 227 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

A weak cool front is at our doorstep early this afternoon. Latest 
radar and sfc obs place the boundary extending between Waco and 
College Stn areas as of early this afternoon. A few showers and 
perhaps some lightning strikes can be expected through the afternoon 
and evening hours as the front slowly sags southward into the region. 
This is a very weak and very slow-moving boundary overall. Current 
forecast suggests it will slowly move over the Houston metro area 
overnight before settling along the coast by early Sunday morning, 
where it will likely meander or even wash out over the coastal 
waters during the day. 

The primary impact from this FROPA will be a temporary drop in 
humidity as drier air filters in from the north. Inland sfc 
dewpoints are forecast to drop into the low 60s to low 70s 
throughout the day on Sunday. Consequently, expect a dry heat across 
most inland locations with high temps climbing into the upper 90s to 
near 100F. A bit of a different story is expected along the coast, 
however. Dewpoint values there will remain in the mid to upper 70s, 
keeping conditions more humid with peak heat indices reaching up to 
107F. Given the close proximity of the boundary near the coast on 
Sunday combined with daytime heating, have maintained low-end PoPs 
for our southwestern counties and coastal zones through the 
afternoon. 

Upper lvl ridging builds back into the region by Monday, setting up 
a return to southerly flow at the surface. In other words, hot and 
humid conditions return with Monday's highs in the upper 90s to near 
102F. Beyond Tuesday, the weather pattern settles into a more 
typical, near-seasonal summertime regime. Expect diurnally-driven, 
isolated showers and storms primarily driven by the daily seabreeze, 
mainly in the each afternoons after Thursday. 

JM

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 602 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

A slowing moving "cold" front continues to push into SE TX this 
evening and overnight. Any remaining showers ahead of the front 
are expected to dissipate in the next couple of hours. In general,
winds veer from WSW to N as the front pushes through. A light and
VRB wind group is included at most TAF sites to account for the 
wind shift associated with the front. At KGLS, elevated and gusty 
winds continue through the evening and overnight. Across all 
sites, a drier air mass arrives in wake of the front, making CIGs 
and VIS a minimal concern. Looking ahead to tomorrow afternoon,
there is a low chance for pop-up showers and thunderstorms 
primarily along the coast due to daytime heating and positioning
of the weak frontal boundary; however, confidence is low. 


MLG

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 227 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

South to southwest winds will gradually strengthen this afternoon and 
evening ahead of an approaching cool front. Building seas are also 
anticipated, mostly remaining up to 5 ft, occasionally higher 
offshore. Small Craft Advisories remain in effect for Galveston Bay 
and nearshore waters from High Island to Freeport through early 
Sunday. The FROPA is expected to reach the bays and coastal waters 
late tonight into Sunday morning. While a brief wind shift to the 
north-northwest will be possible over the bays and nearshore, the 
boundary will meander near the coast through the day; therefore, 
onshore winds will mainly prevail. A few showers and storms will be 
possible this evening and then again Sunday afternoon, depending on 
the final position of the FROPA. Beyond Sunday, dry and hot weather 
is expected with light to occasionally moderate south to southeast 
winds and seas around 2 to 3ft, occasionally up to 4 ft next weekend.

JM

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
605 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Above normal heat continues today with afternoon highs in the
  mid to upper 90s and maximum heat indices of 105-109F. A Heat 
  Advisory remains in affect for Jefferson and Hardin counties in 
  Southeast Texas from 1 PM - 7 PM this afternoon.

- A weak frontal boundary will move through the region tonight
  bringing a 20-60% chance of rain across south central 
  Louisiana.
 
- Some slightly drier air will work into the region Sunday with dewpoints
  falling into the mid to upper 60s, but both high and low 
  temperatures will remain largely unchanged. 

- A few, diurnally driven, afternoon thunderstorms are expected to
  develop each day next week with daily rain chances in the 20-30%
  range. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Friday)
Issued at 1223 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

At the surface, high pressure is in the Gulf while a cold front is 
draped across the Ark-La-Tex from an area of low pressure in 
Illinois. Aloft, upper ridging is over the Four Corners region while 
a trough of low pressure is over the Midwest. As this trough 
progresses south/southeastward today, it will begin to broaden out 
becoming the main feature across the E CONUS as we head towards the 
second half of the weekend. As it does so, it will give the 
aforementioned cold front a further push south towards the coast. As 
this boundary crosses the forecast area this evening/tonight, a 
few showers and/or thunderstorms are expected to develop 
along/ahead of it, particularly over south central LA as it draws
closer to the coast. While this frontal passage will mean very 
little for us temperature wise, with highs still reaching into the
mid-90s tomorrow, it will bring a nice shot of slightly drier air
with a brief north/northwest wind shift tonight through tomorrow.
Tonight, especially as we approach sunrise, dewpoints are 
forecasted to drop into the mid-60s across interior SE TX and 
CENLA. Post sunrise tomorrow, further dry air advection is 
anticipated, with dewpoints at most locations (except near the 
coast) likely not getting above 70 degrees tomorrow. While in the 
grand scheme of things this is not really all that dry, for this 
time of year it should help things to feel far less oppressive 
tomorrow even as highs reach into the 90s. 

Moving into the work week, slow moisture return begins on Monday as 
winds turn back to the W/SW, followed by a more substantial return 
of moisture Mon night into Tuesday as the lingering boundary starts 
to lift off to the north. At the same time, E CONUS upper level 
troughing will begin to weaken and retreat northward, losing its 
hold over the forecast area by late Monday. It may leave behind just 
a slightly weakness aloft over the northern Gulf Coast, between 
ridging that will be slowly building in from the west and east 
simultaneously. With this synoptic set up, a few isolated afternoon 
diurnally driven showers and storms will be possible each
afternoon Tues through late next week. In addition, afternoon 
highs will continue to warm into the mid to upper 90s each day 
with overnight lows in the mid to upper 70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 602 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Conditions will generally prevail VFR through the overnight hours
as winds acquire more WNW - NW components through dawn. As 
frontal boundary moves offshore, there is a chance for VCSH near 
Acadiana terminals, however, guidance is light on any potential 
activity until moving further offshore. VFR conditions will 
prevail through daylight hours of the 02nd under NW flow. 

30

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1223 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

A weak boundary will approach the coastal waters later today, tightening
the pressure gradient overhead. This has already begun to result
in strengthening southwesterly winds, which will continue into
tonight. Tonight into Sunday, westerly winds will increase a bit 
further with sustained 15-20 kts and gusts to 20-25 kts as the 
frontal boundary moves through the coastal waters. The boundary 
will also increase thunderstorm chances late tonight through 
Sunday. An exercise caution statement has been extended through 
Sunday morning and a Small Craft Advisory has also been issued
through late tonight into Sun morning. Light southerly flow 
becomes reestablished Monday through the rest of the week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1223 PM CDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Hot and humid conditions will continue today. Rain chances will 
increase tonight into Sunday as an upper level trough and weak 
frontal boundary approach the area. A brief period of 
northwesterly winds are expected tomorrow, bringing some slightly
drier air into the region. Minimum RH's Sunday and Monday 
afternoons are expected to be in the 35-50% range. Winds will turn
back out of the south Sunday night into Monday. A few 
thunderstorms will develop each afternoon next week. 

&&
